title: Dimension-preserving projective model of a strict localization
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $N\geq0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. Let $x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] of $X$, put $s=f(x)$ and $B=S_{(s)}$, and give $X_{(x)}$ its canonical map to $B$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. There exist a scheme $P$, a projective morphism $p:P\to B$ [def-pc-projective-morphism] which is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], a geometric point $y$ of $P$ over the closed point of $B$, and an isomorphism of $B$-schemes
$$\theta:X_{(x)}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{(y)}.$$
Every scheme-theoretic fibre of $p$ has dimension at most $N$. Neither Noetherianity of $S$ nor finite presentation or quasi-compactness of $f$ is required.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4 in the 28-page author version (the published IMRN version is cited as Proposition 3.1 by Illusie). Read online; local copy WANTED. First reduction paragraph (quasi-finite projection, Zariski main theorem, projective compactification).

proof.text: Put $X'=X\times_SB$ with projections $q:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1) the geometric point $\bar s=f\circ x$ factors through the closed point of $B$ by a canonical lift $\bar s':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$; let $x'=(x,\bar s')$ be the induced geometric point of $X'$, which lies over the closed point of $B$. Fibre bound: let $t\in B$ with image $t_0\in S$ and let $z'\in X'_t$ with image $z\in X_{t_0}$. The fibre-dimension-after-base-change lemma gives $\dim_{z'}(X'_t)=\dim_z(X_{t_0})$, and $\dim_z(X_{t_0})\le\dim X_{t_0}\le N$ (take the open $X_{t_0}$ itself in the definition of $\dim_z$). By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] $\dim X'_t=\sup_{z'}\dim_{z'}X'_t\le N$; so every fibre of $f'$ has dimension at most $N$, and $f'$ is locally of finite type as a base change. Strict localizations: [lem-weil-pbc-strict-base-closed-point-localizations], applied with $\Xi=\Omega$ and $a=\mathrm{id}$ (so $f'x'=\bar s'$ and $\bar u=\bar s$), gives an isomorphism $X'_{(x')}\xrightarrow{\sim}X_{(x)}$ over $X$ which, using $B\cong S_{(\bar s)}$ (here the identity of $B$, by the uniqueness clause (3) of the functoriality lemma), commutes with the maps to $B$. Hence it suffices to prove the lemma for $f':X'\to B$ and $x'$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4: passage to the strict local base and preservation of the fibre-dimension hypothesis.

proof.text: Apply the local quasi-finite projection lemma to the base-changed morphism and the geometric point $x'$ (the scheme $B=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$ is affine by [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]). It gives an affine open $U$ containing the image of $x'$, an integer $d\le N$, and a separated quasi-finite finite-type map $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_B$ over $B$ whose structural composite is the restriction of $f'$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4: first reduction by a quasi-finite projection.

proof.text: The target $\mathbf A^d_B$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Zariski's main theorem in the finite-type separated quasi-finite form therefore factors $e$ as an open immersion $U\hookrightarrow T$ followed by a finite morphism $T\to\mathbf A^d_B$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4: Zariski main theorem reduction.

proof.text: Apply the finite-projective-envelope lemma to $T\to\mathbf A^d_B$. We obtain an open immersion $T\hookrightarrow P$ and a projective proper morphism $p:P\to B$ extending the structural map, with every fibre of $p$ of dimension at most $d$, hence at most $N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4: projective compactification after the finite factorization.

proof.text: Let $y$ be the image of $x'$ under the open immersions $U\hookrightarrow T\hookrightarrow P$; it lies over the closed point of $B$ because $x'$ does and the structural maps to $B$ are compatible ($p\circ j$ restricted to $U$ is $f'|_U$). An open immersion is ind-etale locally on source and target (on an affine open of the target contained in the image, it is an isomorphism of affine schemes). The ind-etale invariance lemma therefore gives isomorphisms over the targets $U_{(x')}\xrightarrow{\sim}X'_{(x')}$, $U_{(x')}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{(x')}$ and $T_{(x')}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{(y)}$; since they commute with the structural maps to $X'$, $T$ and $P$, and $U\to X'\to B$, $U\to T\to P\to B$ agree, they are isomorphisms of $B$-schemes. Composing with the isomorphism of step 1 gives $\theta:X_{(x)}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{(y)}$ over $B$. By step 4, $p$ is projective and proper, and every fibre of $p$ has dimension at most $d\le N$.

source.place: Proposition 2.3, proof, printed p. 4: identification of strict localizations and conclusion.
